A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Stein Diffusion Guidance by the same authors. All 22 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, proofs and experimental appendices, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-generation outcomes, including SDG hit ratios, docking scores, sampling dynamics and validity analyses. Its attribution of external baseline scores does not affect the originality of the SDG results.

after.justification: v2 reports original molecular and image-generation results, component and particle-count ablations, robustness measurements, and runtime and memory benchmarks.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a docking-informed prior over molecular graph order in Appendix C.2, Equation 27, prioritizing graph sizes associated with desirable docking scores. This adds a sampling component, while Algorithm 1 retains the core Tweedie prediction, Stein update, forward noising and reward-guidance procedure. The graph-specific equations are relocated rather than newly introduced.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates molecular generation using ZINC250k and three protein targets. v2 retains this coverage and adds CIFAR-10 label guidance, Gaussian deblurring and image super-resolution from 64×64 to 256×256. These introduce a new data domain and distinct conditional-generation and reconstruction tasks outside low-density molecular sampling.

E2.justification: v2 adds reported image comparisons against DPS and LGD in Table 1, using baseline scores attributed to Ye et al. It also adds molecular comparisons with no-low-density and Langevin-limit SDG variants in Table 2. The original external molecular comparator set remains unchanged; TFG supplies an implementation framework rather than a separate reported comparator.

E3.justification: Reported QuickVina exhaustiveness changes from 8 in v1 Appendix C.6.2 to 1 in v2 Appendix C.2. Molecular schedules and hyperparameters also change, including linear-to-constant annealing for fa7 and 5ht1b. v2 adds FCD/NSPDK evaluation, particle-count controls and image protocols using accuracy, FID and LPIPS. These changes prevent treating the revised molecular scores as identical-setting performance gains.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's no-Stein comparison and edge-density validity sweep, v2 separately tests low-density weighting and the Langevin-limit correction, varies particle counts across 512, 1024 and 3000, and evaluates chemical and structural distribution distances across density levels for all three receptors. It also adds computational analyses and qualitative image comparisons. Existing molecular radar and sampling-dynamics analyses are retained with revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three sampling runs for the principal molecular hit-ratio and top-5% docking tables. v2 introduces no new seed policy, confidence intervals, significance tests or explicit increase in repetitions. Additional molecular ablation rows reuse uncertainty reporting, while the new image results provide point estimates.

E6.justification: Under revised settings, SDG hit ratios for fa7/5ht1b/jak2 change from 1.011/25.744/9.367% in v1 Table 1 to 1.156/22.690/9.167% in v2 Table 2. MOOD's unchanged 9.200% now narrowly exceeds SDG on jak2. Docking scores and plotted results also change. v2 adds substantial image, ablation and computational results, including improved label accuracy but worse FID with Stein correction.

T1.justification: v2 materially revises the posterior-score justification: Lemma 3.3 and Appendix B replace v1's asserted exact expression with an explicit single-sample approximation and correct the Gaussian-score sign in the derivation. Corollary 3.5 adds a Langevin-limit result and proof. v2 also defines the graph-order prior and removes v1's stated O(N^-1/2) particle-convergence guarantee. The central SOC variational bound is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: a low-density SOC cost, a variational argument motivating posterior correction, and Stein correction as an efficient training-free guidance mechanism. The added image evidence broadens support for this framework without redefining the three stated contributions.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's molecular-only validation limitation with discussion of particle-count saturation and unstable high-dimensional SVGD updates. It adds substantive explanations of node-edge coupling, distinct score trajectories and the role of particle interactions. It also discusses image accuracy–FID and runtime tradeoffs. These substantially expand the mechanisms and applicability boundaries discussed, while retaining the reward-overestimation interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the hyperparameter search grid, selected particle counts, graph-prior offset M=10, image implementation choices, DDIM steps, batch size and sampling counts. It adds measured resource requirements and hardware descriptions for molecular and image benchmarks. Reproducibility improves, although Table 7 labels its image configuration with alpha>0 while Appendix D specifies alpha=0.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to Corso et al.'s particle guidance, Song et al.'s LGD, Ye et al.'s TFG and Zhang et al.'s particle-optimization analysis, alongside the LPIPS reference. Several background references, including Berner et al. and Del Moral, are removed. These refine the positioning around particle interactions and guidance methods while retaining the central SOC/SVGD framing.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion, and changes the title. Experiments are reorganized into image and molecular branches; Algorithm 1 and the graph-specific method move to the appendix. Experimental details and visualizations are redistributed into Appendices C–E. This constitutes substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v1's overview figure is split and reworked into v2 Figures 1–2, molecular radar plots are consolidated, and the featured docking image changes. v2 adds image, ablation and computational tables, multi-panel robustness plots and image comparison grids. The three original docking-pose galleries are retained and renumbered. Headers, typography and figure placement also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation: image experiments address v1's explicitly acknowledged molecular-only evidence, while component ablations, particle sensitivity tests and resource measurements make the mechanism and practicality more assessable. The revised posterior-score derivation also exposes its approximation assumption. Results show real tradeoffs rather than universal gains, and changed docking settings plus the image timing-table inconsistency limit some comparisons. Nevertheless, the broader diagnostic evidence and clearer theoretical qualification provide a substantial overall quality improvement.
